reason: The hypothesis relies on combining strengthening from L12/B2 particles (E2) with a ductility mechanism from nanoscale CoCrFeNi (E1), but E1's mechanism is for single-crystalline nanopillars without precipitates, and E3 shows only ~13% elongation with L12/B2 in a different alloy, not supporting improved ductility. No evidence shows this intervention works in HfZrTiTa0.53 or that the mechanism transfers to bulk, precipitate-containing alloys.
premises: Coherent L12 nanoprecipitates and incoherent B2 microparticles can be introduced in HfZrTiTa0.53 to create extreme microstructural heterogeneities.
Extreme microstructural heterogeneities from L12 and B2 particles improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation while preserving strength.
Deformation delocalization and delay of necking failure occur via spatial coordination of deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
The proposed mechanism (twinning + slip coordination) is transferable from nanoscale CoCrFeNi to bulk HfZrTiTa0.53 with L12/B2 particles.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 properties (786 MPa yield, 1314 MPa compressive, 13.5% terminal strain) are from tensile or comparable tests.
